answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to keep a private computational ember—a continuous low-level proof-of-work or unique state that must whisper a fresh attestation into a shared harbor of independent validators. Because the ember cannot be forked or shared without breaking the chain of proofs, an attacker must provision separate dedicated compute cycles for every fake identity, making the cost scale linearly with the number of sybils and eliminating cheap virtual multiplexing.
